theme: Cutting trees that have to grow back
title: Cutting Trees That Have to Grow Back: A Multi-Year Harvest Plan
strategies: positional FIFO: each year cut the first `quota` harvestable cells found in row-major scan order, ignoring value and regrowth entirely (the evaluator's weak reference)

value-greedy / biggest-first: each year cut the `quota` highest-stage cells on the board; wins big in the opening years but, because the maturity threshold equals the value cap, every cut removes a seed source, and once a region's mature trees are gone nothing there ever regrows -- the plan's yield craters over the back half of the horizon

seed-network-preserving harvest: still cut biggest-first by value, but before cutting a mature (stage == S) cell, check whether any not-yet-mature cell within dispersal radius would drop below the seed-count threshold if this cell were removed (accounting for other cuts already committed this year); skip cuts that would break the local seed network and take the next-best cell instead, so a spatially spread set of mature trees survives indefinitely as a renewable seed source

full lookahead / rollout search: simulate several candidate multi-year plans forward (since growth+dispersal+harvest are all deterministic and known) and keep the best by total value; expensive but can match or beat the seed-network heuristic on small boards
